eyebrow: The question every org eventually asks

steps.label: TOO FEW WORKSPACES
steps.sub: one giant workspace — nobody can tell who owns what

steps.label: TOO MANY, UNSTRUCTURED
steps.sub: workspace sprawl — hundreds of flat, unlabeled workspaces

steps.label: THE FIX
steps.sub: a deliberate structure: by team, by lifecycle stage, grouped by domain

caption: Domains (Finance, Health, Education here) group related workspaces by business area — the modern answer to 'how do I organize fifty workspaces.'
Inside the Finance domain, a 'Loans' subdomain narrows the grouping further — useful once a single domain itself has dozens of workspaces.

eyebrow: Three ways to assign at scale
caption: Workspaces join a domain by name, by workspace admin, or by capacity — the capacity option is how an org with dedicated dev/test/prod capacities assigns dozens of workspaces in one action.

steps.label: AVOID GENERIC NAMES
steps.sub: "Reports," "Test," "My Stuff" tell no one anything six months later

steps.label: SET A CONTACT LIST
steps.sub: every workspace should have a named owner, not just an Admin role

eyebrow: Capacity as a structural dimension too
caption: Assigning a workspace to Premium capacity isn't just about performance — separate capacities per dev/test/prod stage is a common, deliberate design pattern.

steps.label: PRODUCTION CONTENT IN 'MY WORKSPACE'
steps.sub: a personal workspace has no shared access model

steps.label: ONE WORKSPACE FOR THE WHOLE COMPANY
steps.sub: flattens RLS, roles, and lifecycle into one undifferentiated pile

steps.label: WORKSPACES WITH NO OWNER
steps.sub: an Admin who left the company, and no contact list to fall back on
